Posterior means or quantiles of a fit, as matrices

Source: R/fit_draws.R
draws_mean.Rd

Summarises the draws of an animal model without the draw dimension, so each covariance matrix is returned as a trait by trait matrix and each trait vector as a named vector. These are the shapes used to compare estimates with a simulated truth, compute heritabilities, or look at a correlation matrix.

Usage

draws_mean(x, parameter = NULL, traits = NULL)

draws_quantile(x, parameter = NULL, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), traits = NULL)

Arguments

x

A fit, or an object from fit_draws.

parameter

Name of the quantity to summarise: "G", "E", "P", "corrG", "corrE", "corrP", "h2", "sigma_G", "sigma_E", "sigma_P", "loadings", "uniqueness", "communality", "genetic_uniqueness", "residual_uniqueness", "s_G", "factor_heritability", "factor_magnitude" or "beta". The default summarises every quantity the fit holds.

traits

Optional trait names, one per trait. The default uses the column names of the response when the fit kept them, and trait1, trait2, ... otherwise.

probs

For draws_quantile, one or more probabilities between 0 and 1; the default is the 95% equal-tailed interval.

Value

For one parameter, a named matrix or vector: k by k for a covariance or correlation matrix, k by the number of terms for beta, and a vector named after the traits for the others. For draws_quantile the last dimension is the quantile, named after the probability. When parameter is NULL, a named list with one summary per quantity.

Details

The summaries are computed from the draws, so the posterior mean of G is the average of the draws and not the covariance of any average. draws_quantile returns the same shapes as draws_mean, with a final dimension for the probabilities.

See also

fit_draws

Examples

k <- 2
vars <- sprintf("G[%d,%d]", rep(1:k, k), rep(1:k, each = k))
m <- cbind(matrix(stats::rnorm(40), 10, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, vars)),
           matrix(stats::rnorm(40), 10, 4,
                  dimnames = list(NULL, sub("G", "E", vars))))
draws_mean(m, "G", traits = c("t1", "t2"))
